newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still mixed late, cash soft.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still mixed late, cash soft.

text.p: NYMEX Hub natgas futures remained mixed late Tuesday in moderate trade, with reports of relatively soft physical prices and forecasts for milder weather by the weekend still undermining sentiment.
At 1410 EST, April was still up by 2.5 cents at $1.84 per million British thermal units, while May was unchanged at $1.865. Most other months were down by 0.2 to 2.7 cents.

"It looks like the weather in early March is pretty mild. There should be plenty of swing gas which should lend more softness to the market, but I think we're within 20 cents of the lows," said one Texas-based trader.

With storage more than adequate to meet any incremental winter load and a mild start predicted for March, most agreed buyers were very relaxed during bidweek this week, a factor that should drive indices almost $1.20 below February 1 levels.

And while some chart traders were looking for a technical correction after the recent dive, few expected much upside without better fundamental backing. They pegged April support at $1.80, then in the mid-$1.70s and then at the contract low of $1.701. Resistance was in the $1.93 area and then at $2.04.

In the cash, February Gulf Coast gas fell five to 10 cents Tuesday to the low-$1.80s, with March on the same pipes talked in the low-to-mid $1.70s. Feb Midcon gas was a few cents lower in the low-$1.70s, with March in the low-to-mid $1.60s. New York city gate gas was talked in the $2.10-2.15 area for Feb and just below $2.10 for March.
NYMEX said 20,905 Hub contracts traded as of 1335 EST.
NYMEX Permian and Alberta natgas were untraded at 1400 EST.
On the KCBT, March was five cents higher at $1.60, while deferreds were up by one to three cents. The East/West spread widened by one cent to 24.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
